energyFlow.title: Energy Flow
energyFlow.engineCaption: Q<sub>h</sub> in splits into W out and Q<sub>c</sub> out.
energyFlow.refrigeratorCaption: W in plus Q<sub>c</sub> in leaves as Q<sub>h</sub> out.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a piston and cylinder on the left and a pressure–volume diagram on the right. A hot reservoir and a cold reservoir dock against the cylinder during the isothermal legs of the cycle, and an insulating sleeve wraps it during the adiabatic legs. A marker traces the same state on the diagram.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has sliders for the two reservoir temperatures, a gas selector, a stage stepper that moves one leg of the cycle at a time, play and speed controls, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Use the stage stepper to walk through the four legs one at a time, and watch where heat enters and leaves.

intro.currentDetails: {{stage}}. Pressure {{pressure}} kilopascals, volume {{volume}} liters, temperature {{temperature}} kelvin.

controls.hotTemperatureHelp: Sets the temperature of the reservoir the gas touches while expanding isothermally.
controls.coldTemperatureHelp: Sets the temperature of the reservoir the gas rejects heat to. Always stays at least 50 kelvin below the hot reservoir.
controls.expansionRatioHelp: How far the gas expands along each isothermal leg. This plus the two temperatures fixes the whole cycle.
controls.gasHelp: Monatomic and diatomic gases have different heat-capacity ratios, which changes the steepness of the adiabatic legs but not the efficiency.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a pressure–volume diagram of the cycle, an energy-flow panel splitting the heat drawn from the hot reservoir into work out and heat rejected to the cold reservoir, and an optional temperature–entropy diagram where the same cycle is a rectangle.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has sliders for the two reservoir temperatures and the expansion ratio, checkboxes for the previous-cycle overlay, the temperature–entropy diagram and the Carnot limit curve, a mode switch between Explore and Measure, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Switch to Measure mode to read the heat and work off the diagram and compute the efficiency yourself before revealing it.

efficiencyLab.currentDetails: Heat in {{qHot}} kilojoules, work out {{work}} kilojoules, heat out {{qCold}} kilojoules. {{efficiency}}
efficiencyLab.efficiencyHidden: Efficiency is hidden until you check your answer.

controls.showPreviousCycle: Show the previous cycle as a ghosted overlay
controls.modeHelp: Explore shows every value live. Measure hides the efficiency until you enter your own and press Check.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the same Carnot cycle run backwards on a pressure–volume diagram, with the arrows reversed, and an energy-flow panel where work in and heat drawn from the cold reservoir both leave as heat delivered to the hot reservoir.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has sliders for the two reservoir temperatures and the expansion ratio, a switch between cooling and heating framing, play and speed controls, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Compare this with the Intro screen: the same four legs, traversed the other way round.

reversedCycle.currentDetails: {{stage}}. Work in {{work}} kilojoules, {{usefulLabel}} {{usefulHeat}} kilojoules, coefficient of performance {{cop}}.

controls.framing: What counts as the useful output
controls.framingHelp: Cooling treats the heat pulled from the cold reservoir as the goal; heating treats the heat delivered to the hot reservoir as the goal.
